revision_changelog: CRITICAL-1 (BLOCKING) FIX — false 'correct on any wave width' claim removed; subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip mandated. The MSG kernel's output coverage is hard-wired to exactly 2 subgroups by the constants 64 (b_tile width, grid divisor N/64) and sg_id*32 (B-read / C-col offset). It MISCOMPUTES on any other wave width: wave64 (sg_size=64) => sg_id=local_x/64=0 for ALL 64 threads => only ONE subgroup runs => C cols [block_col*64+32 .. +64) NEVER written (half of C garbage); SIMD16 (sg_size=16) => sg_id in {0,1,2,3} => sg_id*32 in {0,32,64,96} => OOB read of the 64-wide b_tile AND C col base block_col*64+{64,96} writes into the NEXT workgroup's region (cross-workgroup overwrite race). FIX applied: (1) EC-2 rewritten to state the kernel REQUIRES subgroup_size==32 (one workgroup = exactly 2 32-lane subgroups) and is TYPED-SKIPPED on wave64/SIMD16/other — NOT 'still correct', NOT 'degrades to 1 subgroup'. (2) technical_spec PART-B portability paragraph rewritten to the same honest statement. (3) design_md_additions PART-B rewritten to state the hard sg_size==32 precondition + typed-skip. (4) AT-1743, AT-1744, AT-1750 now MANDATE the subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip guard, mirroring dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510 (`if ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 { eprintln!(... wave64 guard ...); return; }`). (5) The .axc example MUST carry a header comment stating the sg_size==32 (N_SG=2) hard precondition. (6) coder_handoff_notes + EC-2 cite the exact precedent line and accessor (ctx.subgroup_size() -> u32, context.rs:709).

CRITICAL-2 (FOLD-IN) — bit-exactness of the MSG matmul is now stated to be GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION by the emitted workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (execution scope Workgroup=2, memory semantics 0x108 = AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory; emit_workgroup_barrier in subgroup.rs:285-301, unit-tested subgroup.rs:476), NOT merely by AT-1743 passing (which on NVIDIA could pass via near-lockstep luck masking a weaker barrier). There is NO subgroup-scope barrier emission path in the codebase, so the cross-subgroup stage->read sync cannot be accidentally weakened. AT-1743/1744 are the END-TO-END confirmation, not the sole guarantee. AT-1744 (K=48 => 3 K-blocks) explicitly exercises the loop-bottom WAR barrier (before the next k_block overwrites shared) across BOTH subgroups; AT-1743 (K=32 => 2 K-blocks) exercises it once. This is now stated in technical_spec, EC-3, correctness_oracle, and AT-1743/1744 descriptions.

WARNING FOLD-IN (staging-coverage invariant, AT-1620 bug class) — AT-1745 now MUST assert a_block_size % wg_threads == 0 AND b_block_size % wg_threads == 0 (every shared element covered exactly once by the 64 threads via ei=iter*wg_threads+t), in addition to shared_memory_bytes==3072 <= 16384. A new invariant statement added to technical_spec PART-B staging section.

The scanner MUST be a full mirror of body_uses_gid's traversal (emit.rs:457-529). AT-1745 now additionally asserts matmul_msg_coopmat.axc actually emits the LocalInvocationId Input var (body-scanner coverage proof).

WARNING FOLD-IN (non-symmetric fixture for the new 64-wide stride-64 b_tile) — AT-1743/1744 keep the M3.3c non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}); a swapped sg_id offset (subgroup 1 reading subgroup 0's columns) or wrong stride-64 produces max_diff != 0. The new b_tile is 64-wide with row-stride 64 (vs the 32-wide stride-32 in matmul_rb_coopmat.axc) — a NEW shared-layout/stride combination requiring the discriminating fixture.

summary: Two-part milestone. PART A adds the language builtin local_invocation_id(axis: u32) -> u32, lowering to SPIR-V BuiltIn LocalInvocationId (a vec3 u32 Input OpVariable + OpLoad + OpCompositeExtract by literal axis) — IDENTICAL lowering shape to the existing GlobalInvocationId gid() path, NO new SPIR-V capability (LocalInvocationId is core Shader). PART B ships matmul_msg_coopmat.axc: a multi-subgroup (multi-warp) register-blocked coopmat matmul where ONE workgroup contains N_SG subgroups, all threads cooperatively stage a larger shared A/B region, a workgroup barrier syncs ALL subgroups, then each subgroup independently runs its own 2x2 coopmat register block on a distinct output sub-region (subgroup-collective coopmat ops, scope Subgroup). subgroup_id_in_wg = local_invocation_id(0) / subgroup_size() drives the per-subgroup output-tile and shared-read offsets. The kernel REQUIRES subgroup_size==32 (one workgroup = exactly 2 32-lane subgroups): its output coverage is hard-wired to 2 subgroups by the constants 64 (b_tile width / grid divisor N/64) and sg_id*32 (B/C offset), so it MISCOMPUTES on wave64 (half of C unwritten) and SIMD16 (OOB shared read + cross-workgroup C overwrite). The single-subgroup matmul_rb_coopmat.axc + resident_matmul_rb.rs are RETAINED for A/B. TFLOPS reported HONESTLY at 256/512/768 (and 1024 if <50GB) — NO asserted ratio; 'competitive' label only if pct >= 25.0.

technical_spec:
## M3.3d — local_invocation_id() builtin + multi-subgroup matmul

### PART A — local_invocation_id(axis: u32) -> u32 (per-layer lowering)

The builtin mirrors gid() EXACTLY at every layer. gid() is NOT a lexer keyword: it lexes as TokenKind::Ident, parses as Expr::Call{name:"gid"}, and is special-cased in the HIR typechecker's Call arm into HirExprKind::GidBuiltin{axis}, then lowered in codegen as OpLoad(vec3 u32 Input GlobalInvocationId) + OpCompositeExtract(axis). local_invocation_id() follows the identical path with BuiltIn::LocalInvocationId.

**Lexer (token.rs).** No new token kind. local_invocation_id is a plain Ident. Add it to a reserved-builtin-name collision guard (mirror is_reserved_subgroup_builtin) + a unit test. Signature form: local_invocation_id(axis) takes an axis arg exactly like gid(axis) — this is the consistent form (the task confirms gid takes gid(0u32)).

**Parser (parser.rs).** No grammar change. local_invocation_id(0u32) parses as Expr::Call via the existing call-postfix rule. Add parse_local_invocation_id_call test mirroring parse_gid_call.

**HIR (expr.rs + typecheck.rs).** Add HirExprKind::LocalInvocationIdBuiltin{axis: u32} (mirror GidBuiltin). In the typechecker Call arm, dispatch name=="local_invocation_id" to check_local_invocation_id_call (mirror check_gid_call): EXACTLY 1 arg; axis must be an integer literal in 0..=2 (NOT a variable, NOT a non-literal expr — same restriction as gid, validated by the existing tc_gid_axis_* test family which the new tests mirror). Result type ScalarTy::U32. Errors mirror Gid{Arity,AxisOutOfRange,AxisMustBeConstant}. Add the debug pretty-print arm.

**Typecheck result.** local_invocation_id(0u32) : u32, lowered to LocalInvocationIdBuiltin{axis:0}.

**Codegen (buffers.rs + body.rs + emit.rs).**
- buffers.rs: struct LocalInvocationIdVar{var_id, vec3_u32_type_id} + emit_local_invocation_id_variable() mirroring GlobalInvocationIdVar/emit_gid_variable: (1) u32 type, (2) vec3 u32 type, (3) type_pointer Input vec3u32, (4) b.variable(...Input...), (5) b.decorate(var, BuiltIn, [BuiltIn::LocalInvocationId]). NO capability flag set.
- body.rs: KernelResources gains local_id_var: Option<&LocalInvocationIdVar>. emit_local_invocation_id_component(em, axis): OpLoad vec3u32 from var_id; OpCompositeExtract u32 by LITERAL axis (axis is a SPIR-V literal index, NOT a dynamic id — required for static analyzability, exactly like emit_gid_component).
- emit.rs: body_uses_local_invocation_id scanner; emit the var ONLY when the builtin is actually used (do NOT emit-on-buffer-presence like gid does — local_invocation_id is opt-in); add var_id to the OpEntryPoint interface list (Input class).

**Exact SPIR-V emitted for local_invocation_id(axis):**
```
; once per module, in types_global_values:
%u32        = OpTypeInt 32 0
%v3u32      = OpTypeVector %u32 3
%ptr_in_v3  = OpTypePointer Input %v3u32
%localid    = OpVariable %ptr_in_v3 Input
              OpDecorate %localid BuiltIn LocalInvocationId
; at the use site, in the function body:
%vec        = OpLoad %v3u32 %localid
%val        = OpCompositeExtract %u32 %vec <axis>   ; axis is a literal 0|1|2
```
No OpCapability or OpExtension is added. The var_id is appended to the OpEntryPoint GLCompute interface list.

### PART B — multi-subgroup (multi-warp) matmul (matmul_msg_coopmat.axc)

**Goal.** Raise occupancy AND amortize staging by packing N_SG subgroups into ONE workgroup. All N_SG*32 threads cooperatively stage a LARGER shared A/B region; ONE workgroup_barrier synchronizes ALL subgroups; then EACH subgroup independently runs its own 2x2 RB coopmat block on a DISTINCT output sub-region, reading its assigned tiles from the SHARED staged data.

**SHIPPED CONFIG (decided, justified):** @workgroup(64,1,1) -> 2 subgroups of 32 lanes on NVIDIA (N_SG=2). Each subgroup does a 2x2 RB block (32x32 C sub-tile). The 2 subgroups STACK ALONG N: subgroup 0 covers C cols [block_col*64 .. +32), subgroup 1 covers cols [block_col*64+32 .. +64); both cover the SAME 32 rows [block_row*32 .. +32). One workgroup therefore covers a 32x64 C region. Grid = (N/64, M/32, 1).
Justification: N_SG=2 (not 4) keeps register pressure bounded — each subgroup holds 4 coopmat accumulators + ~4 transient coopmats (the proven-safe M3.3c 2x2 footprint), unchanged per-subgroup; the workgroup just has 2 such independent subgroups. 4 accumulators*2 subgroups do NOT share a register file (each subgroup is a separate warp with its own register allocation), so per-warp register pressure is IDENTICAL to single-subgroup RB 2x2 — the proven-safe point. N_SG=2 doubles threads/workgroup (better SM occupancy of warp slots) and HALVES the workgroup count vs single-subgroup RB at the same problem size, while the shared A/B is staged ONCE and reused by BOTH subgroups (staging amortization). Stacking along N (not M) keeps the A row-block shared by both subgroups (both subgroups use the same A rows) -> maximal A-reuse across subgroups; only B differs per subgroup.

**Shared layout (shipped config).** Both subgroups share the SAME 32 A-rows. Stage:
- a_tile: RB_M*16 rows x tile_k cols = 32 x 16 = 512 f16 (1024 B). Shared by BOTH subgroups (identical A region).
- b_tile: tile_k rows x (N_SG*RB_N*16) cols = 16 x 64 = 1024 f16 (2048 B). Covers BOTH subgroups' B columns; subgroup s reads cols [s*32 .. +32).
Total shared = 1024 + 2048 = 3072 B << 16 KB. (a_block_size=512, b_block_size=1024.)

**subgroup_id derivation (uses BOTH new + existing builtins):**
```
let sg_size: u32  = subgroup_size();                       // 32 on NVIDIA — NOT hardcoded
let local_x: u32  = local_invocation_id(0u32);             // 0..63 within the workgroup
let sg_id: u32    = local_x / sg_size;                     // 0 or 1 (which subgroup)
let lane: u32     = subgroup_invocation_id();              // 0..31 within the subgroup
```
**HARD PRECONDITION — subgroup_size MUST be 32 (typed-skipped otherwise, NOT silently correct).** With @workgroup(64,1,1) and sg_size==32, sg_id in {0,1} -> exactly 2 subgroups, which is the ONLY width this kernel is correct for. Although sg_size is read via subgroup_size() (not hardcoded), the kernel's OUTPUT COVERAGE is hard-wired to 2 subgroups by the constants 64 (b_tile width and the grid divisor N/64) and sg_id*32 (the B-read and C-col offset). On any other width the kernel MISCOMPUTES — it is NOT a graceful degrade:
- **wave64 (sg_size=64):** local_x in 0..63 => sg_id = local_x/64 = 0 for ALL 64 threads => only ONE subgroup runs => it writes C cols [block_col*64 .. +32) and reads b_tile cols [0..32), leaving C cols [block_col*64+32 .. +64) NEVER WRITTEN for every workgroup => HALF of C is garbage. (This is NOT 'degrade to single-subgroup RB': single-subgroup RB uses a 32-col grid; the MSG grid is 64-col, so the missing 32 cols are a real, silent coverage hole.)
- **SIMD16 (sg_size=16):** sg_id in {0,1,2,3} => for sg_id in {2,3} the B-read offset sg_id*32 in {64,96} indexes OUT OF BOUNDS of the 64-wide b_tile (OOB shared read) AND the C col base block_col*64+{64,96} lands in the NEXT workgroup's C region => overlapping/racing cross-workgroup C writes.
Therefore the kernel REQUIRES subgroup_size==32, and ALL its dispatch/tests/bench (AT-1743/1744/AT-1750) TYPED-SKIP when ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 (`if ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 { eprintln!(... wave64 guard ...); return; }`), mirroring the existing precedent dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510. The accessor is VulkanContext::subgroup_size() -> u32 (context.rs:709). On NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (wave32, sg_size==32) the guard passes and the tests run; on wave64/SIMD16/other they skip cleanly. The .axc header documents this hard precondition. (A future alternative would be to REQUEST requiredSubgroupSize=32 via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control at pipeline creation — out of scope for M3.3d; the typed-skip is the chosen correctness discipline.)

**Cooperative staging (all 64 threads).** Linear thread index t = local_invocation_id(0u32) (0..63). All 64 threads cooperatively fill a_tile (512 elts) and b_tile (1024 elts):
```
// A: 512 elements, 64 threads -> 8 iters each. ei = iter*64 + t.
//   a_row = ei/16; a_col = ei - a_row*16; A_grow = block_row*32 + a_row; A_gcol = k_block*16 + a_col.
// B: 1024 elements, 64 threads -> 16 iters each. ei = iter*64 + t.
//   b_row = ei/64; b_col = ei - b_row*64; B_grow = k_block*16 + b_row; B_gcol = block_col*64 + b_col.
```
Staging is over ALL threads in the workgroup (t spans 0..63), NOT per-subgroup — this is what amortizes the staging across both subgroups.

**STAGING-COVERAGE INVARIANT (AT-1620 bug class).** The linear-index staging math (ei = iter*wg_threads + t, ei in 0..a_block_size / 0..b_block_size) REQUIRES a_block_size % wg_threads == 0 AND b_block_size % wg_threads == 0 so that every shared element is covered EXACTLY ONCE by the 64 threads (no OOB write at high ei, no gap). Shipped: a_block_size=512 % 64 == 0 -> 8 iters; b_block_size=1024 % 64 == 0 -> 16 iters. AT-1745 asserts both moduli == 0 for the shipped @strategy assignment. A future non-multiple @strategy pick would violate the invariant -> it is an asserted compile-time precondition.

**The barrier across subgroups (CRITICAL correctness).** workgroup_barrier() lowers to OpControlBarrier with EXECUTION scope Workgroup (=2) and MEMORY scope Workgroup + AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory (0x108) — see subgroup.rs EXECUTION_SCOPE_WORKGROUP / MEMORY_SEMANTICS_WORKGROUP_ACQ_REL. Execution scope Workgroup means ALL invocations in the workgroup (BOTH subgroups, all 64 threads) MUST reach the barrier before any proceeds, and the WorkgroupMemory memory semantics make all shared writes visible across subgroups. Therefore after the post-staging barrier, every subgroup sees the COMPLETE staged a_tile/b_tile written by all 64 threads. This is the linchpin: the barrier is a WORKGROUP barrier, not a subgroup barrier, so it correctly synchronizes across subgroups. **BIT-EXACTNESS IS GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION**, NOT merely by AT-1743 passing: emit_workgroup_barrier (subgroup.rs:285-301) emits OpControlBarrier with execution scope Workgroup=2 + memory semantics 0x108 (AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory), unit-tested at subgroup.rs:476 (cg_workgroup_barrier_emits_op_control_barrier_with_scope_2_and_semantics_0x108), and there is NO subgroup-scope barrier emission path in the codebase — so the cross-subgroup stage->read synchronization cannot be accidentally weakened. This matters because on NVIDIA the 2 subgroups of an SM may run in near-lockstep and an end-to-end test alone could pass even with a weaker barrier (the NVIDIA-lockstep-luck hazard); correctness here does NOT rely on the test catching a wrong barrier, because the only barrier the compiler can emit is the correct workgroup-scope one. AT-1743/1744 are the END-TO-END confirmation, not the sole guarantee. The loop-bottom WAR barrier (before the next k_block overwrites the shared tiles) is the SAME workgroup-scope barrier and is exercised only at K>16: AT-1743 (K=32 => 2 K-blocks) hits it once, AT-1744 (K=48 => 3 K-blocks) twice, both across BOTH subgroups. REQUIREMENT: the barrier (and all coopmat ops) must be in UNIFORM control flow across the whole workgroup — the kernel keeps the staging loops, the barrier, the coopmat_load/mul_add/store all at top level with NO subgroup-divergent branching around the barrier (sg_id only selects DATA OFFSETS via arithmetic, never branches around the barrier or the coopmat ops). All 64 threads execute the same control flow; sg_id and lane only feed index arithmetic.

**Per-subgroup coopmat ops (subgroup-collective, scope Subgroup).** VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix: cooperative matrix operations have scope Subgroup — a coopmat value is distributed across the 32 lanes of ONE subgroup, and coopmat_load/mul_add/store are subgroup-collective (all 32 lanes of that subgroup participate). In a 64-thread workgroup with 2 subgroups, EACH subgroup independently executes its own coopmat ops over its own 32 lanes: subgroup 0's coopmat_mul_add operates on subgroup 0's lanes, subgroup 1's on subgroup 1's lanes — they do NOT cross subgroups. This is exactly the intended multi-warp behavior: 2 independent 32-lane coopmat computations in one workgroup. The SHARED data they read is the SAME staged tiles; the OUTPUT tiles differ by sg_id. CONFIRMED: per-subgroup independent execution is the SPIR-V cooperative-matrix semantics (scope = Subgroup), so each subgroup runs its own coopmat block correctly. (See OQ-2 for the residual GPU-verification requirement — AT-1743/1744 are the real-GPU proof.)

**Output-tile and shared-read offsets driven by sg_id (shipped config).** Both subgroups share a_tile (same A rows) and read DIFFERENT B columns from the shared b_tile:
```
// A row-tiles (shared by both subgroups; SAME offsets):
//   a_mat_0 = coopmat_load(a_tile,   0u32, 16u32)   // rows 0..16 of A block
//   a_mat_1 = coopmat_load(a_tile, 256u32, 16u32)   // rows 16..32 of A block
// B col-tiles: subgroup s reads cols [s*32 .. +32) of the 64-wide b_tile (stride 64):
//   b_off0 = sg_id * 32                              // first 16-col band for this subgroup
//   b_off1 = sg_id * 32 + 16                          // second 16-col band
//   b_mat_0 = coopmat_load(b_tile, b_off0, 64u32)   // stride = N_SG*RB_N*16 = 64 (full b_tile width)
//   b_mat_1 = coopmat_load(b_tile, b_off1, 64u32)
// Accumulators (4, loop-carried, SAME N-phi path as M3.3c — NO codegen change):
//   acc_00 += a_mat_0*b_mat_0 ; acc_01 += a_mat_0*b_mat_1 ; acc_10 += a_mat_1*b_mat_0 ; acc_11 += a_mat_1*b_mat_1
// Output C coordinates (subgroup s writes a 32x32 block at row block_row*32, col block_col*64 + s*32):
//   c_col_base = block_col*64 + sg_id*32
//   tile_row_0 = block_row*2 ; tile_row_1 = block_row*2 + 1
//   col_tile_0 = c_col_base/16 ; col_tile_1 = c_col_base/16 + 1   (or compute c_base directly)
//   c_base_ij = (tile_row_i*16)*N + (c_col_base + j*16) ; coopmat_store(acc_ij, C, c_base_ij, N)
```
The sg_id*32 offset into shared b_tile and into C columns is the ONLY thing that distinguishes the two subgroups — pure index arithmetic, NO divergent branching.

**4 loop-carried coopmat accumulators per subgroup — NO codegen change.** Each subgroup carries acc_00..acc_11 (4 coopmats) across the K-loop. detect_loop_carried_coopmat + the N-phi single-loop path (AT-1733, locked in M3.3c) already emits 4 OpPhis in one loop header. Because all 64 threads execute the SAME loop with the same trip count, and each subgroup's coopmat ops are subgroup-collective, the per-subgroup accumulators are correct. NO codegen change for the matmul (the ONLY codegen change in M3.3d is the local_invocation_id builtin).

**@strategy holes (genuinely parameterized).** @strategy { wg_threads: ?[64], n_sg: ?[2], rb_m: ?[2], rb_n: ?[2], tile_k: ?[16], a_block_size: ?[512], b_block_size: ?[1024] }. wg_threads drives @workgroup and the staging iteration counts (a_block_size/wg_threads, b_block_size/wg_threads). n_sg drives the b_tile width (N_SG*RB_N*16) and the bench grid (N/(N_SG*RB_N*16), M/(RB_M*16), 1). rb_m/rb_n drive the per-subgroup block (hand-unrolled to 2x2; OQ-1). tile_k fixed 16 (coopmat K dim). a/b_block_size drive shared tile sizes. As in M3.3c, the holes select among PRE-WRITTEN unrolled variant files (hand-unroll boundary — OQ-1); but they genuinely drive shared sizes + bench grid.

**Bit-exactness oracle.** RB tiling + multi-subgroup tiling change ONLY the LOOP/TILE STRUCTURE and which subgroup computes which output tile — NOT the numeric op sequence per output tile. Each acc_ij accumulates the SAME ordered coopmat_mul_add over the SAME K-blocks as the single-tile/single-subgroup kernel for that output tile -> bit-identical. Verified by AT-1743 (M=32,N=64,K=32, grid (1,1,1), 1 workgroup = 2 subgroups, max_diff==0) and AT-1744 (M=64,N=128,K=48, grid (2,2,1), 3 K-blocks, max_diff==0) on the non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}; detects A/B index/offset swaps — a swapped sg_id offset on the new 64-wide stride-64 b_tile yields max_diff != 0; a symmetric fixture MUST NOT be substituted). The cross-subgroup correctness is guaranteed BY CONSTRUCTION by the workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (above); AT-1743/1744 are the end-to-end confirmation. BOTH tests carry the subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip guard (the kernel requires sg_size==32; see HARD PRECONDITION above) AND typed-skip on Lavapipe (CoopMatUnsupported).

**TFLOPS expectation (HONEST reasoning).** Multi-subgroup CAN beat single-subgroup RB 2x2 (24.96% at 768) via two effects: (1) higher SM occupancy — 64-thread workgroups fill warp slots better and the grid is HALF the workgroup count at the same size, but each workgroup does 2x the work; net warps-in-flight is comparable but staging is shared; (2) staging amortization — the A row-block is staged ONCE and reused by BOTH subgroups (vs twice in two separate single-subgroup workgroups). Against it: (a) the workgroup barrier now synchronizes 64 threads / 2 subgroups (slightly higher barrier latency than 32-thread); (b) b_tile doubled (2048 B) but still tiny; (c) at small sizes the grid shrinks further (768 -> grid (12,24,1)=288 WGs vs RB's (24,24,1)=576) which could UNDER-occupy. HONEST prediction: a MODEST improvement at >=512 (staging amortization + better warp occupancy), possibly crossing 25% (competitive) at 768/1024; at 256 likely a regression (too few workgroups), reported honestly like M3.3c. The acceptance gate is honest improvement at the BEST measured size vs 31.2 TFLOPS — and an HONEST report if barrier/occupancy interplay caps it at or below single-subgroup RB. NO asserted ratio. The single-subgroup RB bench is retained for direct A/B at every size.

correctness_oracle: Bit-exact (max_diff == 0.0) vs cpu_f16_matmul_reference on the non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, K-sum f16-integer-exact). Rationale: multi-subgroup + register tiling changes only loop/tile structure and output-tile assignment, NOT the per-tile ordered coopmat_mul_add sequence, so each output tile is bit-identical to the single-subgroup/single-tile kernel. Cross-subgroup correctness is additionally GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION by the emitted workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (scope Workgroup=2, semantics 0x108; subgroup.rs:285-301, unit-tested subgroup.rs:476) — no subgroup-scope barrier path exists to weaken it. AT-1743 (1 workgroup, 2 subgroups, 2 K-blocks) and AT-1744 (4 workgroups, 3 K-blocks, 2 WAR barriers) are the end-to-end GPU proofs, and BOTH carry the subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip guard (the kernel REQUIRES sg_size==32 and miscomputes otherwise). For local_invocation_id(): AT-1742 is an EXACT-integer GPU oracle (out[g*64+l]==l). No @equiv_fp_tol needed (integer-exact f16 path).
edge_cases: EC-1 N_SG not dividing the C-N extent: grid uses ceil only via exact-multiple fixtures (N multiple of N_SG*RB_N*16 = 64). Partial/edge tiles (N or M not a multiple of 64/32) are OUT OF SCOPE (carried-forward masked/predicated coopmat from M3.3b) — the bench/tests use exact multiples; the grid pre-check asserts divisibility and the example documents the constraint.

EC-2 subgroup_size != 32 — HARD PRECONDITION, TYPED-SKIPPED (NOT silently correct): the MSG kernel REQUIRES subgroup_size==32 (one workgroup = exactly 2 32-lane subgroups). Its output coverage is hard-wired to 2 subgroups by the constants 64 (b_tile width / grid divisor N/64) and sg_id*32 (B-read / C-col offset), so it MISCOMPUTES on any other wave width and is NOT a graceful degrade: (a) wave64 (sg_size=64): sg_id = local_x/64 = 0 for ALL 64 threads => only ONE subgroup runs => C cols [block_col*64+32 .. +64) NEVER written for every workgroup => HALF of C is garbage (NOT 'degrade to single-subgroup RB' — the MSG grid is 64-col-per-WG, so the missing 32 cols are a real silent coverage hole). (b) SIMD16 (sg_size=16): sg_id in {0,1,2,3} => B-read offset sg_id*32 in {64,96} is OOB of the 64-wide b_tile (OOB shared read) AND C col base block_col*64+{64,96} writes into the NEXT workgroup's region (cross-workgroup overwrite race). BECAUSE these are correctness-fatal, the kernel does NOT run on non-32 widths: AT-1743/1744/AT-1750 carry the subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip guard `if ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 { eprintln!(... wave64 guard ...); return; }` (mirror dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510; accessor VulkanContext::subgroup_size() -> u32, context.rs:709). NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 = wave32 (sg_size==32) -> the guard passes, N_SG=2, tests run. On wave64/SIMD16/other -> clean typed-skip. The .axc header documents the precondition. (Alternative requiredSubgroupSize=32 via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control is out of scope for M3.3d.)

EC-3 workgroup barrier across subgroups (bit-exact GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION): workgroup_barrier() lowers (emit_workgroup_barrier, subgroup.rs:285-301, unit-tested subgroup.rs:476) to OpControlBarrier execution scope Workgroup=2 + memory semantics 0x108 (AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory), so ALL 64 threads (both subgroups) sync and all staged shared writes are visible cross-subgroup. There is NO subgroup-scope barrier emission path in the codebase, so the cross-subgroup stage->read sync CANNOT be accidentally weakened — bit-exactness is guaranteed by this emitted barrier, not merely by AT-1743 passing (which on NVIDIA could pass via near-lockstep luck). The kernel keeps the barrier in UNIFORM control flow (sg_id feeds only index arithmetic, never branches around the barrier or coopmat ops) — required for defined behavior. The loop-bottom WAR barrier (before the next k_block overwrites shared) is the SAME workgroup-scope barrier, exercised at K>16 by AT-1743 (2 K-blocks) and AT-1744 (3 K-blocks). AT-1743/1744 are the end-to-end real-GPU confirmation.

EC-4 per-subgroup coopmat execution: coopmat ops have scope Subgroup; each 32-lane subgroup runs its own coopmat block on its own lanes independently. No cross-subgroup coopmat sharing. The shared-read offset (sg_id*32) ensures each subgroup reads its assigned B columns from the SHARED b_tile. AT-1743/1744 verify on real GPU.

EC-5 register pressure: per-subgroup footprint is the proven-safe M3.3c 2x2 (4 acc + ~4 transient coopmats); 2 subgroups do NOT share a register file (separate warps), so per-warp pressure is UNCHANGED from single-subgroup RB. Shared doubled to 3072 B (still << 16 KB). If a future N_SG=4 or rb 4x4 spills, the bench measures and the honest best wins; the shipped config is the safe point.

EC-6 occupancy at small sizes: at 256 the msg grid is (4,8,1)=32 WGs of 64 threads (vs RB's 64 WGs of 32). Fewer workgroups may under-occupy; reported honestly (like M3.3c's 256 regression). 50 GB cap + 2D grid pre-check on both axes asserted before allocation.

EC-7 local_invocation_id emitted only when used: unlike gid (emitted on buffer presence), local_invocation_id var is emitted ONLY when the builtin is called (body_uses_local_invocation_id) — avoids an unused Input var in kernels that don't use it; keeps the interface list minimal.
open_questions: OQ-1 (hand-unroll boundary, carried from M3.3c): AXIOM has no compile-time strategy-unroll and no coopmat array type (coopmats are SSA, not addressable). The 2x2-per-subgroup x N_SG=2 config is HAND-UNROLLED (named accumulators acc_00..acc_11; sg_id is index arithmetic, not a loop over subgroups). @strategy holes drive shared sizes + bench grid but the unroll is fixed per variant file. A strategy-unroll / coopmat-array language feature would let N_SG/RB be true holes — future work, NOT this milestone.

OQ-2 (per-subgroup coopmat correctness — RESOLVED by spec + by-construction barrier, GPU-CONFIRMED by AT): VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix scope is Subgroup, so each 32-lane subgroup independently executes its coopmat ops; the cross-subgroup stage->read sync is guaranteed BY CONSTRUCTION by the workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (subgroup.rs:285-301), not merely by a test passing. The multi-subgroup design is sound per spec. AT-1743/1744 are the mandatory real-GPU confirmation (anti-pattern #9), gated on subgroup_size()==32 (the kernel's hard precondition): if a driver mis-handles 2 subgroups/workgroup with coopmat, max_diff != 0 would catch it. NO multi-subgroup TFLOPS or bit-exact claim ships until AT-1743/1744 pass on NVIDIA (sg_size==32).

OQ-3 (does multi-subgroup beat single-subgroup RB?): HONEST open question resolved by AT-1750 measurement. Expected modest gain at >=512 from staging amortization + warp occupancy, possibly crossing 25% at 768/1024; possible regression at 256. If barrier/occupancy interplay caps it at or below 24.96%, that is reported HONESTLY and the milestone still ships (the local_invocation_id builtin is the durable deliverable; the kernel is the honest A/B). NO asserted ratio.

OQ-4 (stacking along N vs M): shipped config stacks subgroups along N so both share the A row-block (max A-reuse). An M-stacked variant (share B col-block) is symmetric; N-stacking chosen because it also keeps the C stores contiguous-ish per row. Either is expressible; N-stacking ships.
coder_handoff_notes: ONLY ONE codegen change for the language: the local_invocation_id() builtin (buffers.rs var + body.rs lowering arm + emit.rs wiring + HIR expr/typecheck + lexer/parser tests). The matmul needs NO codegen change — it reuses the M3.3c N-phi loop-carried-coopmat path (AT-1733 locked) and the shared/coopmat emit paths.

EVERY GPU test/bench for it (AT-1743/1744/AT-1750) MUST guard `if ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 { eprintln!("...: subgroup_size={} != 32; skipping (wave64 guard)", ctx.subgroup_size()); return; }` BEFORE allocation/dispatch — copy the exact pattern from dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 (AT-1510). ## 3.1.18 M3.3d — local_invocation_id() builtin + multi-subgroup (multi-warp) coopmat matmul

M3.3c (§3.1.17) reached 31.2 TFLOPS = 24.96% of the 125-TFLOPS datasheet estimate at 768 via 2x2 register blocking, SINGLE-subgroup-per-workgroup. The next gain is MULTI-subgroup blocking: a workgroup with N_SG subgroups, each computing distinct output tiles while SHARING the staged A/B in workgroup memory -> higher occupancy AND amortized staging. This needs a builtin AXIOM lacked: local_invocation_id().

**PART A — local_invocation_id(axis: u32) -> u32.** A new HIR builtin lowering to SPIR-V BuiltIn LocalInvocationId (a vec3 u32 Input OpVariable + OpLoad + OpCompositeExtract by literal axis) — IDENTICAL lowering shape to gid() (GlobalInvocationId). LocalInvocationId is a CORE Shader builtin: NO new SPIR-V capability, NO extension (anti-pattern #7: no silent capability). Threaded through lexer (plain Ident, like gid), parser (Expr::Call, no grammar change), HIR (HirExprKind::LocalInvocationIdBuiltin{axis}, typecheck: arity 1, axis literal 0..=2, result u32), codegen (emit_local_invocation_id_variable in buffers.rs + emit_local_invocation_id_component in body.rs + emit.rs wiring; emitted ONLY when used). AT-1740 (lex/parse/HIR/typecheck), AT-1741 (codegen + spirv-val + no-new-capability), AT-1742 (real-GPU bit-exact: out[g*64+l]==l).

**PART B — matmul_msg_coopmat.axc (multi-subgroup, SHIPPED N_SG=2).** @workgroup(64,1,1) = 2 subgroups of 32 lanes. subgroup_id_in_wg = local_invocation_id(0u32) / subgroup_size(). HARD PRECONDITION: the kernel REQUIRES subgroup_size==32 (one workgroup = exactly 2 32-lane subgroups). Its output coverage is hard-wired to 2 subgroups by the constants 64 (b_tile width / grid divisor N/64) and sg_id*32 (B/C offset), so it MISCOMPUTES on other wave widths and is NOT a graceful degrade: wave64 (sg_size=64) -> sg_id=0 for all threads -> only ONE subgroup runs -> half of C (cols +32..+64 per WG) NEVER written; SIMD16 (sg_size=16) -> sg_id in {0,1,2,3} -> sg_id*32 OOB of the 64-wide b_tile + cross-workgroup C overwrite. Therefore ALL its GPU tests/bench TYPED-SKIP when subgroup_size()!=32 (mirror dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510); on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (wave32) they run. Both subgroups SHARE the same staged 32-row A block (max A-reuse); they STACK ALONG N, each computing a 2x2 RB block (32x32 C sub-tile) on its own B columns (subgroup s reads shared b_tile cols [s*32..+32); writes C cols [block_col*64 + s*32 .. +32)). All 64 threads cooperatively stage a_tile[512]/b_tile[1024] (3072 B shared; a/b_block_size % wg_threads == 0 so every element is covered exactly once); ONE workgroup_barrier. **Cross-subgroup bit-exactness is GUARANTEED BY CONSTRUCTION** by the emitted workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (execution scope Workgroup=2, memory semantics 0x108 AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory; emit_workgroup_barrier subgroup.rs:285-301, unit-tested subgroup.rs:476) — there is NO subgroup-scope barrier path to weaken it, so this does not rely on a test passing via NVIDIA lockstep luck. Each subgroup then independently runs its coopmat block (coopmat scope = Subgroup -> per-32-lane-subgroup execution). 4 loop-carried coopmat accumulators per subgroup via the M3.3c N-phi path (AT-1733) — NO codegen change for the matmul. Grid = (N/64, M/32, 1). @strategy holes wg_threads/n_sg/rb_m/rb_n/tile_k/a_block_size/b_block_size genuinely drive shared sizes + bench grid (hand-unrolled per OQ-1).

**Bit-exact.** AT-1743 (M=32,N=64,K=32, grid (1,1,1) = 1 WG = 2 subgroups, 2 K-blocks, max_diff==0) + AT-1744 (M=64,N=128,K=48, grid (2,2,1), 3 K-blocks => 2 WAR barriers, max_diff==0) on the non-symmetric integer-f16 fixture (catches a swapped sg_id offset on the 64-wide stride-64 b_tile). The workgroup-scope barrier guarantees cross-subgroup correctness by construction; AT-1743/1744 are the end-to-end confirmation and BOTH carry the subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip guard. Single-subgroup AT-1731/1732 RETAINED. Typed-skip on Lavapipe (CoopMatUnsupported) AND on subgroup_size()!=32.

**Measured TFLOPS (AT-1750) — HONEST, no asserted ratio.** resident_matmul_msg.rs (M3.3c methodology) at 256/512/768 (+1024 if <50GB). Reports BARE tflops + pct of 125-TFLOPS; competitive label only if pct>=25.0. Single-subgroup RB bench RETAINED for A/B. Expected: modest gain at >=512 from staging amortization + warp occupancy (possibly crossing 25% at 768/1024); possible 256 regression. If barrier/occupancy interplay caps it, reported HONESTLY — the local_invocation_id builtin is the durable deliverable regardless. [QA fills measured numbers here.]

**Deferred to M3.4+.** Double-buffered shared staging (software pipelining); partial/edge tiles (M,N not multiples of 64/32 — masked coopmat); N_SG=4 / true strategy-unroll over N_SG and RB (needs coopmat-array / strategy-unroll language feature, OQ-1).
